title: Just ask
hook: du'a is asking Allah directly, any time, in any language

segments.voice: Yesterday: qurbani, the sacrifice of Eid al-Adha, shared three ways. Your line was a third for the poor.

One kind of prayer in Islam has no required form at all. No set words. No set language. No set time. You don't even need to face anywhere. You just talk. For weeks, this path has been teaching forms: the exact Arabic words, where the hands go, how many times to say glory, how many units at dawn. All that precision has a counterweight, and this is it.
screen: `ONE PRAYER WITH NO FORM AT ALL.` → `YOU JUST TALK.` → `AFTER WEEKS OF EXACT FORMS.`

segments.voice: The word is du'a, from an Arabic root that means to call, the way you'd call someone's name across a room. The salat, the five daily prayers, is the fixed form: set times, set movements, set words in Arabic. Du'a is the open one: asking Allah for something, directly, whenever you want. In Arabic, in English, in Urdu, in the half-sentences you'd use at three in the morning. In the usual view, it doesn't need wudu, a prayer mat, or a particular direction, though people often face the qiblah and raise their hands. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gave it a surprising rank. Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi report him saying: du'a is worship itself. Then he recited a verse, Surah Ghafir, forty, sixty: And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer. Not a formal request through the proper office. Pray unto Me. And the times it seems nothing happens? The hadith collections are honest about that. Bukhari reports that a person's du'a is answered as long as they don't grow impatient and say, I prayed and prayed and nothing came. A hadith in the Musnad of Ahmad says that a du'a asking for nothing sinful, and not for cutting family ties, is answered in one of three ways: given now, saved for the next life, or a harm of the same size quietly turned away. In that teaching, no such du'a is wasted. It may come back in a shape nobody ordered. Which leaves only the hard part: actually asking.
screen: `DU'A — TO CALL.` · `SALAT IS FIXED; DU'A IS OPEN.` · `DU'A IS WORSHIP ITSELF.` · `ANSWERED IN ONE OF THREE WAYS.` · then, large: `JUST ASK.`

segments.voice: Find the thing you actually want, not the polite version, small or large: sleep, a good conversation tomorrow, the test results. Put it into one plain sentence; if you pray, say it to Allah, in any language, out loud or silently, and if you don't, say it to yourself and notice how it feels to admit you want it. Then sit with it, and don't add anything.
Du'a. Calling on Allah directly, any time, in any language, asking for what you need. Today's word.
Your line: no du'a is wasted. Any language, any hour, any words. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 130 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHEN THE HEART IS HEAVY.`

howItsDone: Muslims make du'a at any time and in any language, often after the salat or with hands raised, asking Allah directly for their own needs and for others.

fork.setup: you've asked for the same thing for months, and nothing seems to change. what does the hadith in Bukhari warn against?
options: growing impatient and saying 'I prayed and nothing came'
fork.reveal: a du'a is answered as long as the person doesn't grow impatient and give up (Bukhari). the warning is about quitting, not about how you ask.

original.note: Arabic: calling, supplication, from the root d-'-w, to call.

trapdoor: what you thought: Muslim prayer is all set words in Arabic.
what it means: the salat is fixed, but du'a is open: any time, any language, your own words.
what a scholar hears: 'du'a is worship' (Abu Dawud 1479; Tirmidhi 2969), followed by 40:60; and the three answers (Ahmad).
